patterns.what_worked: Reading the audit's file:line rows before touching anything kept the fixes minimal and in-scope; wiring F2 to the existing offhand-presence probe (check_weapons) instead of deleting the handler gave a real production path; moving both ends of the offhand cycle (start + ends_at) avoided introducing a negative bar span; the mutation harness on /tmp/opencode copies proved every fix is held by a pin (10/10 killed, each by a named check).
patterns.what_was_hard: The audit's F2 note named the flag but not the class dimension: a paladin or druid has an offhand weapon and NO offhand bar, so wiring has_oh alone would have made the handler touch frames that were never created (and AceDB's '**' metatable would have synthesised the missing hand table). That needed a new ST:has_hand() helper and a class-parameterised test fixture.
patterns.skill_gap: The first F3 mutation was killed by a Lua syntax error rather than by a pin - a mutant that fails to parse proves nothing about the pin. Every mutation now has to fail on a named check, not on a load error.
